vocalProfiles.name: Obsidian Profundo
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre family: Cinematic pop, dark folk, industrial, ambient rock
Era: 1980s–modern
Origin cue: International film-score and dark studio production
Voice: Bass/profundo
Target range: C2–E4
Register: Predominantly chest; controlled upper mix
Resonance: Chest and pharyngeal
Vibrato: Slow, restrained, 4–5.5 Hz
Ornamentation: Sustained low notes, deliberate slides, spoken-sung endings
Mix: Large and authoritative without turning the low mids muddy

Plugin prompt — “Obsidian Profundo”

Build a solo male bass vocal processor. Use a microphone character like a Neumann U47 or M49. Apply an 18 dB/oct high-pass filter at 42 Hz; dynamic de-boom reduction from 140–240 Hz, maximum -3 dB; bell boost +2 dB at 1.2 kHz, Q 1.0; presence +1 dB at 3.5 kHz; de-esser from 5.5–7.5 kHz. Add Fairchild 660-style compression at 2:1, 25 ms attack, 250 ms release, targeting 2–4 dB GR. Add 10% tape saturation and a 0.8-second dark chamber with 25 ms pre-delay and 7% wet mix. Keep everything below 180 Hz mono.

Knobs: Sub Weight, Word Edge, Iron, Room
Macro: Gravity raises 100–180 Hz weight, compression and tape saturation together
Presets: Cinematic Depth, Dark Folk Bass, Industrial Low

Suno style text:
solo male profundo bass, extremely low chest resonance, controlled dark tone, deliberate phrasing, restrained vibrato, cinematic authority, dry studio intimacy

vocalProfiles.name: Velvet Bass-Baritone Crooner
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Traditional pop, jazz, orchestral ballad
Era: 1940s–1960s
Origin cue: New York and Los Angeles studio orchestras
Voice: Bass-baritone
Range: E2–G4
Resonance: Warm chest with forward diction
Vibrato: Smooth, regular, 5–6 Hz
Ornamentation: Portamento, delayed consonants, gentle scoops
Mix: Vocal stays above the arrangement without excessive brightness

Plugin prompt — “Velvet Crooner”

Create a bass-baritone crooner chain like a Neumann M49 into a tube console. High-pass at 55 Hz; low shelf +1.5 dB at 120 Hz; mud cut -2 dB at 280 Hz, Q 1.2; diction boost +1.5 dB at 2.2 kHz; air shelf +1 dB at 10 kHz. Use LA-2A-style optical compression for 2–3 dB GR. Add 5% tube saturation, a vintage plate reverb with 1.5-second decay, 45 ms pre-delay and 10% mix, plus a filtered 95 ms slap at 7% mix.

Knobs: Velvet, Smile, Slap, Plate
Macro: Supper Club adds warmth, plate and gentle compression
Presets: Velvet Close, Orchestra Lead, Noir Crooner

Suno style text:
solo male bass-baritone crooner, polished legato, warm chest resonance, precise diction, controlled traditional vibrato, intimate studio orchestra character

vocalProfiles.name: Midnight Narrator
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Spoken-sung alternative, trip-hop, noir pop
Era: 1990s–modern
Voice: Low baritone
Range: E2–F♯4
Register: Speech-dominant chest register
Resonance: Close, dark and forward
Vibrato: Minimal
Ornamentation: Vocal fry entrances, whispered endings, pitch inflection
Mix: Almost completely dry and centered

Plugin prompt — “Midnight Narrator”

Build a close spoken-sung baritone chain like an Electro-Voice RE20 or Shure SM7B. High-pass at 65 Hz; dynamic proximity control from 100–220 Hz, maximum -4 dB; cut -2.5 dB at 320 Hz; diction boost +3 dB at 1.8 kHz; low-pass at 15 kHz. Use an 1176-style compressor at 4:1, 8 ms attack, 120 ms release, 4 dB GR. Add a mouth-click remover for events 0.2–8 ms long and a 0.35-second room at 4% mix.

Knobs: Proximity, Diction, Stillness, Shadow
Macro: Closer increases low-mid intimacy and reduces room mix
Presets: Noir Close, Spoken Melody, Dry Documentary

vocalProfiles.name: Candlelight Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Intimate pop, singer-songwriter, bedroom folk
Era: 1970s–modern
Voice: Warm baritone
Range: G2–G4
Resonance: Chest-forward with soft upper harmonics
Vibrato: Narrow and occasional
Ornamentation: Breathy onsets, gentle cracks, falling phrase endings
Mix: Preserve breaths and room detail without exaggerating noise

Plugin prompt — “Candlelight Baritone”

Create an intimate baritone chain with a Neumann U67 or Coles 4038-style softness. High-pass at 70 Hz; warmth +1.5 dB at 180 Hz; cut -2.5 dB at 320 Hz; dynamic harshness reduction from 2.5–4.5 kHz, maximum -2.5 dB; air shelf +1.5 dB at 10 kHz. Apply LA-2A-style compression for 2–3 dB GR and 8% tape saturation. Add a 0.75-second wooden room with 12 ms pre-delay and 8% mix. Keep tuning slower than 50 ms or disabled.

Knobs: Close, Wood, Breath, Ease
Macro: Candlelight adds warmth, soft compression and room
Presets: Bedroom 2AM, Wooden Room, Barely Processed

vocalProfiles.name: Clean High Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Pop, alternative pop, clean rock
Era: 1990s–modern
Voice: High baritone
Range: A2–B4
Register: Chest into connected mix
Resonance: Balanced chest and facial mask
Vibrato: Controlled, medium width
Ornamentation: Clean scoops and modest sustained notes
Mix: Neutral enough to work across multiple genres

Plugin prompt — “High Baritone Standard”

Build a clean high-baritone channel like a Neumann U87 through an API preamp. High-pass at 80 Hz; cut -2 dB at 250 Hz; dynamic honk suppression from 800 Hz–1.2 kHz; presence +2 dB at 3.2 kHz; air +2 dB at 11 kHz. Compress at 3:1 with 12 ms attack, 90 ms release and 4 dB GR. De-ess from 6.5–8 kHz. Add a 1.2-second plate with 35 ms pre-delay and 10% mix.

Knobs: Body, Focus, Air, Control
Macro: Finished raises focus, compression and air
Presets: Clean High Baritone, Pop Neutral, Rock Clear

vocalProfiles.name: Bright Pop Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Mainstream pop, dance-pop, pop-rock
Era: 2000s–modern
Voice: Lyric tenor
Range: C3–C5
Resonance: Forward mask with clean upper mix
Vibrato: Narrow and controlled
Ornamentation: Quick runs, clean flips, sustained hook notes
Mix: Highly polished and present but not piercing

Plugin prompt — “Pop Radio Tenor”

Create a polished pop-tenor chain like a Sony C-800G into a Tube-Tech CL 1B. High-pass at 95 Hz; cut -2.5 dB at 220 Hz; dynamic harshness control from 2.8–4.5 kHz; presence +3 dB at 5 kHz; high shelf +3 dB at 12.5 kHz. Compress at 3:1, 8 ms attack, 80 ms release, 4–6 dB GR. De-ess around 7.2 kHz. Use natural pitch correction at 20–35 ms. Add a 1.6-second plate, 70 ms pre-delay, 14% mix and filtered dotted-eighth delay at 12%.

Knobs: Polish, Clarity, Tune, Halo
Macro: Pop Radio increases compression, air and delay ducking
Presets: Pop Radio, Clean Verse, Glossy Hook

vocalProfiles.name: Power-Ballad Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Rock ballad, power pop, dramatic pop
Era: 1980s–2000s
Voice: Tenor/baritenor
Range: B2–C♯5
Resonance: Chest-dominant mix opening into head resonance
Vibrato: Wide and dramatic on sustained notes
Ornamentation: Long notes, controlled breaks, octave leaps
Mix: Verses restrained; climaxes expand without clipping

Plugin prompt — “Power Tenor Lift”

Build a two-stage power-tenor chain like a Neumann U67 into an 1176 and LA-2A. High-pass at 85 Hz; dynamic cut from 180–350 Hz, maximum -3 dB; boost +2 dB at 2 kHz; +3 dB at 4.5 kHz; shelf +2 dB at 10 kHz. First compressor: 4:1, 5 ms attack, 120 ms release, 3 dB GR. Second optical compressor: 2 dB GR. Add a vintage plate at 2.2 seconds, 65 ms pre-delay, 18% mix. Add automatic +2 dB rides to sustained notes, followed by a -1 dBTP limiter.

Knobs: Chest, Lift, Sustain, Plate
Macro: Final Chorus opens the air, increases sustain and expands the reverb
Presets: Restrained Verse, Power Chorus, Dramatic Bridge

vocalProfiles.name: Airy Falsetto
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Pop, intimate R&B, dream pop
Era: 1970s–modern
Voice: High tenor falsetto/head voice
Range: E3–E5
Resonance: Head-dominant, light and airy
Vibrato: Narrow, floating
Ornamentation: Register flips, breath releases, descending runs
Mix: Add body without making the falsetto sound artificial

Plugin prompt — “Falsetto Cloud”

Build an airy male falsetto processor. High-pass at 120 Hz; add +2 dB body at 220 Hz, Q 0.8; cut -1.5 dB at 1 kHz; dynamic sibilance reduction from 6–9 kHz, maximum -5 dB; shelf +2 dB at 14 kHz. Compress at 2:1, 20 ms attack, 160 ms release, 2 dB GR. Add a gentle breath expander below -45 dB at 1.5:1. Add a 2.6-second shimmer plate, 90 ms pre-delay, 10% wet.

Knobs: Body, Feather, Air, Cloud
Macro: Float increases air, stereo reverb and soft compression
Presets: Airy Hook, Intimate Falsetto, Dream Head Voice

vocalProfiles.name: Art-Pop Countertenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Art pop, chamber pop, electronic experimental
Era: 1970s–modern
Voice: Countertenor/head-dominant male voice
Range: G3–E5
Resonance: Head, mask and upper pharyngeal space
Vibrato: Precise and intentionally exposed
Ornamentation: Classical turns, long straight tones, controlled slides
Mix: Unusual and elevated but recognizably human

Plugin prompt — “Glass Countertenor”

Create a countertenor processor with AKG C12 or Neumann U67 character. High-pass at 110 Hz; cut -2 dB at 350 Hz; boost +2 dB at 1.6 kHz; dynamic control from 3–5 kHz, maximum -3 dB; air shelf +1.5 dB at 12 kHz. Use slow optical compression for 2.5 dB GR. Add a 1.8-second chamber, 50 ms pre-delay, 12% mix. Pitch correction should remain slower than 40 ms to protect intentional vibrato.

Knobs: Glass, Human, Vibrato Protect, Chamber
Macro: Art Form increases chamber depth, upper-mid focus and sustain
Presets: Glass Solo, Chamber Voice, Electronic Countertenor

vocalProfiles.name: Silky R&B Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Contemporary R&B, pop-soul
Era: 1990s–modern
Voice: Smooth tenor
Range: C3–C5
Resonance: Forward and rounded
Vibrato: Controlled; delayed at note endings
Ornamentation: Melisma, falsetto transitions, gentle scoops
Mix: Close and expensive with smooth high frequencies

Plugin prompt — “R&B Silk”

Build a silky R&B tenor chain like a Sony C-800G into a Neve 1073 and Tube-Tech CL 1B. High-pass at 90 Hz; warmth +1 dB at 180 Hz; cut -2 dB at 250 Hz; presence +2.5 dB at 4 kHz; shelf +2 dB at 12 kHz. Compress at 3:1, 10 ms attack, 100 ms release, 4 dB GR. De-ess at 6.8 kHz. Add same-source microshift at -6/+6 cents with 12/18 ms delays and 8% mix. Plate: 1.8 seconds, 55 ms pre-delay, 12% mix.

Knobs: Silk, Body, Double, Late Night
Macro: Slow Jam adds warmth, widening and plate
Presets: R&B Lead, Silky Hook, Dry Run

vocalProfiles.name: Smoky Neo-Soul Baritenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Neo-soul, alternative R&B, jazz-soul
Era: 1970s and 1990s–modern
Voice: Baritenor
Range: A2–A4
Resonance: Chest-rich with softened mask resonance
Vibrato: Loose, conversational
Ornamentation: Behind-the-beat scoops, blue notes, gentle rasp
Mix: Warm, rounded and slightly aged

Plugin prompt — “Neo-Soul Smoke”

Create a smoky baritenor processor like a Neumann U67 through a Neve 1073. High-pass at 75 Hz; shelf +2 dB at 140 Hz; cut -2 dB at 350 Hz; presence +1 dB at 2.2 kHz; gentle low-pass at 14 kHz. Use LA-2A-style compression for 3–5 dB GR and 12% tube saturation. Add a 0.9-second spring at 10% and an eighth-note tape delay at 8%, filtered from 450 Hz–5 kHz.

Knobs: Smoke, Pocket, Tube, Spring
Macro: After Hours increases tube saturation, delay and low-mid warmth
Presets: Neo-Soul Lead, Smoky Verse, Warm Falsetto

vocalProfiles.name: Solo Soul Belter
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Soul, blues-soul, pop-soul
Era: 1960s–modern
Voice: Baritenor/tenor
Range: A2–C5
Resonance: Chest and forward mask
Vibrato: Strong and deliberate
Ornamentation: Melisma, growled attacks, sustained belts
Mix: Dynamic and emotional without turning into a choir sound

Plugin prompt — “Soul Fire”

Build a solo soul-belter chain like a Neumann M49 into an 1176 and Fairchild. High-pass at 85 Hz; dynamic de-mud at 250 Hz, maximum -3 dB; boost +2 dB at 1.5 kHz and +3 dB at 3.5 kHz; dynamic de-harsh from 2.5–5 kHz. First compressor: 1176-style, 8:1, 3 ms attack, 90 ms release, 3–5 dB GR. Second: Fairchild-style, 2:1, 2 dB GR. Blend 20% parallel compression. Add a 1.7-second vintage plate at 14% mix.

Knobs: Fire, Testimony, Control, Plate
Macro: Open Up raises parallel compression, presence and plate
Presets: Soul Lead, Controlled Belt, Raw Testimony

vocalProfiles.name: Funk Precision Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Funk, disco-funk, rhythmic pop
Era: 1970s–modern
Voice: Light tenor/high baritone
Range: B2–B4
Resonance: Bright, forward and percussive
Vibrato: Minimal except sustained endings
Ornamentation: Staccato syllables, yelps, rhythmic falsetto flips
Mix: Tight and rhythmically locked, never group-like

Plugin prompt — “Funk Precision”

Create a rhythmic male funk-vocal chain like a Shure SM7B into an API preamp and dbx 160. High-pass at 100 Hz; cut -3 dB at 250 Hz; boost +2 dB at 1.2 kHz and +3 dB at 4.5 kHz. Compress at 4:1, 5 ms attack, 80 ms release, 4 dB GR. Add a downward expander with -42 dB threshold and 150 ms release. Add a 75 ms filtered slap and a 0.4-second studio room.

Knobs: Bite, Pocket, Snap, Slap
Macro: On The One tightens the gate, compression and slap
Presets: Dry Funk, Falsetto Funk, Rhythmic Pop

vocalProfiles.name: Fragile Indie Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Style Profile

Genre: Indie pop, bedroom pop, dream folk
Era: 2000s–modern
Voice: Light tenor
Range: C3–B4
Resonance: Light nasal mask with airy edges
Vibrato: Unstable by design but not digitally warped
Ornamentation: Voice cracks, soft scoops, unfinished phrase endings
Mix: Preserve vulnerability and natural level variation

Plugin prompt — “Indie Fragile”

Build a delicate indie-tenor processor with Neumann U67 softness. High-pass at 100 Hz; cut -2 dB at 300 Hz; add +1.5 dB at 1.8 kHz; dynamic de-ess from 6.5–8.5 kHz. Use 15% tape saturation and gentle 2:1 compression at 30 ms attack, 180 ms release, 2 dB GR. Add a 1.1-second wooden room with 20 ms pre-delay and 9% mix. Same-source microshift should remain below 5%.

Knobs: Fragile, Tape, Breath, Window
Macro: Bedroom adds subtle tape, room and softness
Presets: Bedroom Close, Indie Clear, Dreamy Dry

vocalProfiles.name: Low Dry Rap Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Modern rap; low baritone; G2–E4; chest-dominant resonance; almost no vibrato; deliberate consonants and low inflection.

Plugin prompt — “Low Rap Authority”

Build a dry baritone rap chain like a Shure SM7B into a Neve 1073. High-pass at 70 Hz; chest boost +2 dB at 120 Hz; cut -3 dB at 280 Hz; diction +3 dB at 2 kHz; presence +2 dB at 5 kHz; low-pass at 16 kHz. Use 1176-style compression at 4:1, 8 ms attack, 100 ms release, 4–6 dB GR. Blend 15% parallel compression. Room must be no longer than 0.25 seconds and no more than 2% wet.

Knobs: Authority, Diction, Clamp, Dry
Macro: Front Row increases presence and parallel compression
Presets: Dry Low Rap, Heavy Verse, Spoken Threat

vocalProfiles.name: Boom-Bap Gravel Rap
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: 1980s–2000s hip-hop; baritone; G2–G4; gritty chest resonance; no sung vibrato; hard consonants and deliberate breath placement.

Plugin prompt — “Boom-Bap Gravel”

Build a rugged rap chain like a U87 or RE20 through a Neve 1073. High-pass at 75 Hz; boost +2 dB at 140 Hz; cut -3 dB at 350 Hz; presence +2 dB at 3 kHz; high shelf -1 dB above 10 kHz. Use an 1176 at 8:1, 5 ms attack, 120 ms release, 5 dB GR. Add 15% tape saturation and 25% parallel compression. Add a 0.45-second dark room at 5%.

Knobs: Gravel, Chest, Crush, Dust
Macro: Head Nod raises tape, parallel compression and 140 Hz weight
Presets: Golden Era, Gravel Center, Sampled Darkness

vocalProfiles.name: Modern Punch Rap
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Contemporary rap; high baritone/tenor; A2–A4; forward mask; straight tone; tightly timed attacks and clean phrase endings.

Plugin prompt — “Modern Punch”

Create a modern rap-vocal chain like a Sony C-800G through an API preamp and Empirical Labs Distressor. High-pass at 90 Hz; cut -2 dB at 200 Hz; dynamic de-mud at 350 Hz; boost +3 dB at 3.5 kHz; shelf +2.5 dB at 11 kHz. Compress at 6:1, 4 ms attack, 80 ms release, 5 dB GR. De-ess at 7.5 kHz. Add a -1 dBTP limiter and automatable delay throws filtered from 500 Hz–6 kHz.

Knobs: Punch, Focus, Ess, Throw
Macro: Record Ready increases focus, limiting and short parallel compression
Presets: Modern Clean, Punch Verse, Delay Throw

vocalProfiles.name: Rapid Technical Rap
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Technical and rapid rap; tenor/high baritone; crisp speech register; minimal vibrato; rapid consonants, internal rhymes and controlled breath gaps.

Plugin prompt — “Syllable Lock”

Build a fast-articulation rap processor. High-pass at 100 Hz; cut -2 dB at 180 Hz; dynamic control from 250–500 Hz; diction boost +4 dB at 2.8 kHz; dynamic de-esser from 5.5–8 kHz. Use 1176-style compression at 4:1, 2 ms attack, 60 ms release, 3 dB GR. Add a transient articulation band from 1–4 kHz with a maximum +2 dB attack enhancement. Room: 0.2 seconds, 1–2% wet.

Knobs: Syllables, Breath Gap, Speed Clamp, Focus
Macro: Machine Precision tightens compression and articulation enhancement
Presets: Fast Clean, Dense Verse, Dry Technical

vocalProfiles.name: Dark Drill Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Drill and dark trap; 2010s–modern; London/Chicago/New York color cue; low baritone; E2–F4; stern chest resonance; nearly monotone delivery.

Plugin prompt — “Drill Shadow”

Build a dark drill vocal chain like a close SM7B. High-pass at 65 Hz; shelf +2 dB at 100 Hz; notch -3 dB at 250 Hz; presence +2 dB at 1.5 kHz; low-pass at 9 kHz. Add 12% transistor saturation. Compress at 4:1, 10 ms attack, 110 ms release, 5 dB GR. Optional pitch correction: 15–30 ms. Add a 120 ms dark slap filtered from 400 Hz–3.5 kHz at 8% mix.

Knobs: Shadow, Weight, Threat, Slap
Macro: Cold darkens the top, increases saturation and shortens ambience
Presets: Dark Drill, Cold Monotone, Low Threat

vocalProfiles.name: Melodic Trap Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Melodic trap; 2010s–modern; Atlanta/Memphis production cue; tenor; B2–C5; chest-to-head transitions; pronounced tuned slides and sustained notes.

Plugin prompt — “Melodic Trap Lock”

Build a tuned melodic-trap chain. High-pass at 100 Hz. Pitch correction: 0–8 ms retune for hard mode, 15–25 ms for melodic mode, humanize 5–15%, formant shift from 0 to -1 semitone. Cut -2.5 dB at 250 Hz; presence +3 dB at 3.2 kHz; air +2 dB at 11 kHz. Use CL 1B-style compression at 3:1, 7 ms attack, 85 ms release, 5 dB GR. Add dotted-eighth delay at 12%, dark plate at 1.4 seconds and same-source microshift at ±7 cents.

Knobs: Tune Speed, Formant, Drip, Space
Macro: Trap Ready tightens tuning, raises air and widens the microshift
Presets: Trap Ready, Melodic Glide, Natural Trap

vocalProfiles.name: Cracked Emo-Rap Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Emo rap and alternative trap; tenor; C3–C5; vulnerable chest/head breaks; narrow vibrato; cracks, breath catches and unstable emotional endings.

Plugin prompt — “Cracked Melody”

Build an emotional melodic-rap chain. High-pass at 95 Hz; warmth +2 dB at 180 Hz; cut -2 dB at 400 Hz; dynamic harshness control from 2.5–4.5 kHz. Tune at 8–18 ms while preserving intentional breaks. Compress at 4:1, 8 ms attack, 120 ms release, 4 dB GR. Add 10% warm tube saturation, a 2.4-second plate with 75 ms pre-delay and an eighth-note delay filtered above 5 kHz.

Knobs: Crack Protect, Pain, Tune, Rain
Macro: Broken Hook increases saturation, tuning and reverb
Presets: Fragile Verse, Cracked Hook, Dry Confession

vocalProfiles.name: Whisper Trap Vocal
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Intimate trap and alternative rap; high baritone/tenor; whispered chest/head blend; straight tone; close breaths and low-volume tension.

Plugin prompt — “Whisper Trap Close”

Build a close whisper-rap chain like an SM7B recorded 2–4 inches away. High-pass at 120 Hz; body +2 dB at 200 Hz; cut -3 dB at 500 Hz; intelligibility +3 dB at 4 kHz; de-ess from 6–9 kHz. Blend 30% parallel compression while keeping the main compressor at 2:1, 20 ms attack and 140 ms release. Use a 0.7-second dark room and 1/8-note delay, both ducked 5 dB by the dry vocal with 250 ms release.

Knobs: Whisper, Body, Breath Protect, Dark Space
Macro: Inside Your Head increases proximity, parallel compression and dark delay
Presets: Close Whisper, Dark Secret, Intimate Trap

vocalProfiles.name: Distorted Alternative Rap
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Industrial rap, experimental hip-hop and trap-rock; high baritone/tenor; speech-to-shout range; pitch drops, whispered sections and controlled distortion.

Plugin prompt — “Broken Circuit Rap”

Build a three-band distorted rap processor. Keep frequencies below 180 Hz clean and mono. Apply 15–35% tube/transistor distortion from 180 Hz–4 kHz. Apply only 5–10% bit reduction above 4 kHz. Add an optional -12-semitone parallel pitch layer at 8% and a +7-semitone texture at 3%. Gate the processed paths at -42 dB with 5 ms attack and 120 ms release. Compress the final output at 4:1, 3 ms attack, 90 ms release.

Knobs: Circuit, Low Ghost, Digital Teeth, Clean Blend
Macro: Malfunction raises distortion, pitch layers and gating intensity
Presets: Broken Verse, Industrial Rap, Controlled Glitch

vocalProfiles.name: Folk Storyteller
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Folk and singer-songwriter; 1960s–modern; baritone/tenor; G2–A4; natural chest resonance; restrained vibrato; conversational phrasing.

Plugin prompt — “Folk Storyteller”

Build a natural solo folk-vocal chain like a Neumann U67 or Coles 4038. High-pass at 75 Hz; cut -2.5 dB at 250 Hz; dynamic control from 2.5–4 kHz, maximum -2 dB; shelf +1 dB at 10 kHz. Use optical compression for only 2 dB GR. Add a 0.8-second wooden room with 15 ms pre-delay and 8% mix. Disable hard tuning and preserve timing variation.

Knobs: Story, Wood, Honesty, Distance
Macro: Front Porch Studio adds warmth and a restrained wooden room
Presets: Storyteller Close, Dry Folk, Wooden Room Solo

vocalProfiles.name: High-Lonesome Solo Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Bluegrass-adjacent folk and acoustic roots; high tenor; C3–D5; bright nasal-mask resonance; mostly straight tone; upward scoops and held vowels. No harmony singers.

Plugin prompt — “High Lonesome Solo”

Create a solo high-folk-tenor processor with RCA 77 or U67 smoothness. High-pass at 100 Hz; cut -2 dB at 250 Hz; boost +2 dB at 1.4 kHz; dynamic pluck-like harshness suppression from 3–4.5 kHz; shelf +1 dB at 9 kHz. Compress at 3:1, 15 ms attack, 160 ms release, 3 dB GR. Add a 1.1-second chamber at 8%. Do not create harmony layers.

Knobs: Lonesome, Nasal Focus, Smooth, Chamber
Macro: Mountain Air increases mid focus and chamber depth
Presets: Solo High Folk, Acoustic Lead, No Harmony

vocalProfiles.name: Country Twang High Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Country and country-pop; 1950s–modern; Nashville/Texas color cue; high baritone; A2–B4; forward twang; delayed vibrato and note scoops.

Plugin prompt — “Country Twang Lead”

Build a solo country vocal chain like a Neumann U47 into an LA-2A. High-pass at 85 Hz; cut -2.5 dB at 300 Hz; boost +2 dB at 1.2 kHz and +2 dB at 3.5 kHz; de-ess around 7 kHz. Use a fast 1176-style compressor for 2 dB peak control followed by 2–3 dB optical compression. Add a 110 ms tape slap at 9% and a 1.1-second plate at 7%.

Knobs: Twang, Chest, Slap, Polish
Macro: Country Radio increases diction, slap and controlled air
Presets: Modern Country, Vintage Twang, Acoustic Country

vocalProfiles.name: Blues-Roots Rasp
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Blues, roots rock and folk-blues; baritenor; G2–B4; chest-heavy resonance; loose vibrato; controlled rasp, blue-note slides and cracked attacks.

Plugin prompt — “Roots Rasp”

Create a rough solo blues vocal with RCA 77 or SM7B character. High-pass at 70 Hz; boost +2 dB at 160 Hz; cut -2 dB at 400 Hz; boost +3 dB at 1.8 kHz; dynamic harshness control from 3–5 kHz; roll off gently above 12 kHz. Blend 25% parallel tube saturation. Compress at 3:1, 12 ms attack, 140 ms release, 4 dB GR. Add a 0.9-second spring reverb at 10%.

Knobs: Rasp, Roots, Tube, Spring
Macro: Weathered raises grit and warmth while reducing high-frequency polish
Presets: Roots Lead, Weathered Blues, Clean Rasp

vocalProfiles.name: Classic Rock Tenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Classic and blues rock; 1960s–1980s; tenor/baritenor; A2–C5; chest-forward mix; medium-wide vibrato; sustained belts and gritty note entrances.

Plugin prompt — “Classic Rock Lead”

Build a classic-rock vocal chain like a Neumann U67 into an 1176. High-pass at 80 Hz; cut -2.5 dB at 250 Hz; boost +2 dB at 1.6 kHz and +2.5 dB at 3.5 kHz; shelf +1.5 dB at 10 kHz. Compress at 4:1, 5 ms attack, 100 ms release, 5 dB GR. Add 15% tape saturation, a 1.8-second plate at 13%, and a 100 ms slap at 6%.

Knobs: Rock Chest, Edge, Tape, Plate
Macro: Lead Guitar Rival increases presence, compression and saturation
Presets: Classic Lead, Rock Ballad, Dry Rasp

vocalProfiles.name: Grunge Gravel Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Alternative rock and grunge; late 1980s–1990s; Pacific Northwest color cue; baritone; F2–A4; chest/pharyngeal resonance; unstable vibrato; breathy verses and gravelly peaks.

Plugin prompt — “Grunge Gravel”

Create a close aggressive rock chain like an SM7B into an 1176 and tape machine. High-pass at 75 Hz; boost +2 dB at 180 Hz; dynamic mud control around 300 Hz; boost +3 dB at 2.2 kHz; dynamic harshness clamp from 3–6 kHz, maximum -5 dB. Compress at 8:1, 2 ms attack, 90 ms release, 6 dB GR. Add 20% tape saturation and a 0.7-second dirty room at 10%.

Knobs: Gravel, Chest, Bleed, Dirty Room
Macro: Loud Quiet Loud increases saturation and compression while opening room ambience
Presets: Grunge Verse, Gravel Chorus, Unplugged Dark

vocalProfiles.name: Pop-Punk Nasal High Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Pop-punk and alternative rock; 1990s–2000s; West Coast/Midwestern U.S. cue; high baritone; A2–B4; nasal mask resonance; narrow vibrato; scoops and urgent phrase attacks.

Plugin prompt — “Pop-Punk Bite”

Build a solo pop-punk vocal chain like a Shure SM7B through an API preamp. High-pass at 100 Hz; cut -3 dB at 250 Hz; boost +2 dB at 900 Hz and +4 dB at 3.2 kHz; de-ess at 7 kHz. Compress at 4:1, 3 ms attack, 70 ms release, 6 dB GR. Add 2 dB soft clipping, an 85 ms slap at 7%, and a 0.7-second plate at 8%. Never add gang vocals.

Knobs: Nasal Bite, Urgency, Clip, Slap
Macro: Hook Energy increases bite, clipping and slap
Presets: Pop-Punk Lead, Urgent Verse, Clean Hook

vocalProfiles.name: Machine-Room Dynamic Tenor/High Baritone
vocalProfiles.p:
Expanded version of your example

Style Profile

Genre family: Industrial rock, alternative rock, electronic rock
Era: 1990s
Origin: Chicago/Cleveland studio color cue
Voice: Tenor/high baritone
Range: Approximately G2–C5
Register: Complete range deployment—spoken chest, whisper, mixed belts, head voice and processed scream
Resonance: Chest-to-head movement with deliberately extreme changes
Vibrato: Precise and dramatic; withheld until key sustained notes
Ornamentation: Distorted screams, whispers, broken phrase endings, pitch drops and massive sustained notes
Diction: Intimate and nearly internal in quiet sections; cutting and over-articulated in loud passages
Dynamic architecture: Near silence followed by controlled walls of vocal sound
Mixing philosophy: The vocal becomes part lead singer, part synthesizer and part percussion instrument

Plugin prompt — “Machine Room Morph”

Build an industrial male-vocal super-plugin with two parallel vocal paths and extreme automation capability.

Quiet Path: microphone character like a Neumann U87; high-pass at 70 Hz; warmth +2 dB at 180 Hz; cut -2.5 dB at 350 Hz; compressor at 3:1, 15 ms attack, 180 ms release, 3 dB GR; dark tape saturation at 7%; 0.45-second room at 5%.

Aggressive Path: microphone character like a Shure SM7B; high-pass at 95 Hz; cut -4 dB at 250 Hz; boost +4 dB at 2.7 kHz; dynamic harshness control from 3.5–7 kHz, maximum -6 dB. Add an 1176-style compressor at 12:1, 0.8 ms attack, 60 ms release, targeting 8–12 dB GR. Distort only 500 Hz–4 kHz with 20–55% drive; keep frequencies below 160 Hz clean.

Add parallel pitch layers: -12 semitones at 8% mix, +7 semitones at 3% mix and ±9-cent microshift at 7%. Add a digital ring-modulation texture adjustable from 15–40 Hz at no more than 5% mix. Include an industrial-noise input that opens only while the vocal is active, using -38 dB threshold, 2 ms attack and 100 ms release.

Add two spaces: 0.35-second metallic room for aggression and 2.5-second dark plate for exposed notes. Both reverbs must duck 6 dB during active singing and recover in 300 ms.

Include section automation that can move from -12 dB intimate phrases to +8 dB aggressive walls without clipping. Add a final -1 dBTP limiter.

Knobs: Warmth, Cut, Damage, Pitch Ghost, Metal Room, Dark Plate
Primary macro: Pressure crossfades from warm U87 intimacy to compressed SM7B distortion
Secondary macro: Human↔Machine increases pitch layers, ring modulation, noise and spectral distortion
Third macro: Silence↔Wall controls level rides, compression intensity, stereo width and reverb size
Presets: Machine Whisper, Controlled Breakdown, Industrial Wall, Sustained Damage, 1990s Digital

Suno style text

Solo male tenor/high-baritone industrial alternative-rock vocal, 1990s Midwestern studio character, extreme quiet-to-loud dynamics, warm close whispers contrasted with harsh cutting belts and controlled distorted screams, precise dramatic vibrato on selected sustained notes, digital processing and industrial texture integrated into the single lead voice, vocal functioning as part singer and part sound design.

vocalProfiles.name: Alternative-Metal Clean-to-Scream
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Alternative metal; 1990s–2010s; high baritone/tenor; G2–C5; clean chest/mix passages contrasted with solo distorted peaks.

Plugin prompt — “Clean/Rage Morph”

Build two parallel paths. Clean path: U87 character, high-pass 80 Hz, cut -2 dB at 280 Hz, presence +2 dB at 3 kHz, 3:1 compression at 12 ms attack and 130 ms release. Rage path: SM7B character, high-pass 100 Hz, dynamic cut from 250–450 Hz, boost +3 dB at 1.8 kHz, dynamic harshness control from 3–6 kHz, 8:1 compression at 1 ms attack and 70 ms release. Add 20% mid-band saturation and a 0.6-second room.

Knobs: Clean, Rage, Harsh Control, Room
Macro: Morph crossfades between the clean and distorted paths
Presets: Clean Verse, Heavy Chorus, Balanced Metal

vocalProfiles.name: Metalcore Fry-Scream Processor
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Metalcore and modern heavy rock; 2000s–modern; high baritone/tenor; fry-like distortion; intense forward resonance; minimal vibrato.

Plugin prompt — “Fry Control”

Build a solo harsh-vocal processor. High-pass at 100 Hz; cut -4 dB at 250 Hz; boost +3 dB at 1.5 kHz; dynamic harshness reduction from 2.5–5 kHz, maximum -6 dB; de-ess from 6–9 kHz. Compress at 8:1, 1 ms attack, 70 ms release, 8 dB GR. Add 15% tube saturation and a 0.45-second concrete room at 8%. Include a 30% clean parallel path to preserve words.

vocalProfiles.name: Death-Growl Processor
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Death metal and extreme industrial; bass/baritone; approximately C2–E4; low pharyngeal resonance; no conventional vibrato; growls and guttural articulation.

Plugin prompt — “Abyss Growl”

Build a low-growl processor like an RE20 or SM7B into a Distressor. High-pass at 55 Hz; shelf +2 dB at 90 Hz; cut -4 dB at 220 Hz; boost +3 dB at 900 Hz for words; boost +2 dB at 2.5 kHz; low-pass at 10 kHz. Compress at 6:1, 5 ms attack, 100 ms release, 6 dB GR. Add 20% saturation and a 0.3-second dark room. Keep the fundamental centered and mono below 180 Hz.

Knobs: Abyss, Words, Grind, Depth
Macro: Monster Focus raises 900 Hz articulation with saturation and low weight
Presets: Readable Growl, Deep Industrial, Dry Guttural

High-pass at 140 Hz; cut -3 dB at 400 Hz; boost +3 dB at 2.8 kHz; dynamic harshness suppression from 4–8 kHz, maximum -7 dB; de-ess at 7 kHz. vocalProfiles.name: Hardcore Solo Shout
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Punk and hardcore; baritone/high baritone; chest-dominant projected voice; straight tone; explosive attacks. Always one vocalist—never gang shouts.

Plugin prompt — “Solo Shout”

Build a single-vocalist hardcore processor like an SM7B. High-pass at 90 Hz; cut -3 dB at 250 Hz; boost +3 dB at 1.5 kHz and +3 dB at 4 kHz. Compress at 8:1, 2 ms attack, 90 ms release, 7 dB GR. Blend 20% parallel soft clipping. Add a 0.5-second dry studio room at 6%. Do not generate group vocals or unison layers.

Knobs: Shout, Words, Clip, Room
Macro: Solo Impact raises compression, articulation and clipping
Presets: Hardcore Solo, Punk Lead, Studio Shout

vocalProfiles.name: Electronic Vocoder/Formant Voice

Profile: Synth-pop, industrial pop, electronic R&B; any male register; intentionally robotic but rhythmically articulate.

Build a 16/24-band vocoder and formant processor. Pre-filter the vocal with a 100 Hz high-pass and de-esser from 6–9 kHz. Vocoder range: 100 Hz–8 kHz; analysis attack 8 ms; release 90 ms. vocalProfiles.name: Theatrical Cinematic Baritenor
vocalProfiles.p:
Profile: Theatrical rock, cinematic pop and dramatic ballads; baritenor; G2–C5; full chest-to-head deployment; precise vibrato; sustained notes and dramatic pauses.

vocalProfiles.name: Spoken-Word Male Voice
vocalProfiles.p:

Knobs: Truth, Proximity, Diction, Stillness
Macro: Documentary increases intelligibility, level consistency and subtle room

Universal Male Vocal Artifact-Removal Plugin

vocalProfiles.name: Vocal Artifact Surgeon
vocalProfiles.p:
Create an adaptive restoration plugin specifically for generated or stem-separated male vocals.

Stage 1 — Rumble and plosives: Use a variable high-pass filter from 25–120 Hz. Detect plosives in the 20–160 Hz region with 5 ms attack, 80 ms release and maximum 6 dB reduction.

Stage 2 — Click/crackle repair: Detect discontinuities from 0.1–8 ms. Interpolate only the damaged samples and preserve consonant attacks.

Stage 3 — De-warble: Analyze pitch stability over a 60–350 ms window. Correct unintended motion up to ±25 cents while protecting intentional vibrato between 4.5–7.5 Hz.

Stage 4 — De-swirl: Smooth watery spectral movement from 1.5–9 kHz with adjustable 0–60% strength. Never flatten the complete vocal spectrum.

Stage 5 — Metallic resonance control: Use dynamic notches from 2.2–6.5 kHz, Q 6–14, maximum -5 dB reduction.

Stage 6 — Phantom-voice suppression: Preserve the center lead. Gate side-channel vocal energy from 250 Hz–6 kHz at -38 dB threshold, 5 ms attack and 220 ms release. Preserve stereo air above 9 kHz.

Stage 7 — Ghost syllable detector: Identify repeated or overlapping fragments occurring 20–150 ms after the original consonant. Attenuate them by 3–12 dB without shortening the real word.

Stage 8 — Tail cleanup: Reduce generated reverb decay by 20–60%; use a -48 dB tail threshold and 250 ms release.

Stage 9 — Final protection: Apply transparent de-essing from 5–9 kHz and a -1 dBTP limiter.

Suno artifact-removal/regeneration prompt

Use this when creating an alternate vocal take:

Regenerate only the solo male lead vocal as a clean, isolated, studio-recorded stem. Preserve the original melody, timing, register, emotional dynamics, diction and phrase lengths. Remove watery spectral artifacts, metallic ringing, digital warble, unstable formants, clipped consonants, repeated syllables, phantom harmonies, background voices, smeared transients, excessive breath noise and artificial reverb. Complete every word naturally. One singer only, center-focused, dry and artifact-free. No choir, chant, crowd, gang vocal, call-and-response, live ambience or newly generated backing singers.

vocalProfiles.name: Solo Male Vocal Engineer
vocalProfiles.p:
Create an adaptive male-vocal mixing plugin that listens to at least three seconds of incoming audio before processing.

Detect bass, bass-baritone, baritone, high baritone, tenor or head-dominant vocal behavior.
Detect whether the performance is spoken, rapped, sung, whispered, belted or intentionally distorted.
Auto-gain the input to approximately -18 dBFS average with peaks between -10 and -6 dBFS.
Set the high-pass filter automatically between 45–120 Hz.
Use dynamic EQ for mud from 180–450 Hz, honk from 700 Hz–1.4 kHz, harshness from 2.5–6 kHz and sibilance from 5–9 kHz. Never cut more than 5 dB per band.
Select compression automatically: 2–3 dB GR for intimate singing, 4–6 dB for pop and rap, or 6–10 dB for distorted rock.
Detect BPM and choose 1/16, 1/8, dotted-1/8 or 1/4-note delay.
Select a room between 0.25–0.9 seconds, plate between 1.1–2.5 seconds or remain completely dry.
Detect artifacts before compression so generated noise is not made louder.
Prevent additional voices, chant-like layers and side-channel phantom vocals.
Finish with an output ceiling of -1 dBTP.

Prompt

Create a mono vocal plugin called “Close Whisper Frame.” Base it on a Neumann U87 into a Neve 1073 and LA-2A-style opto compressor.

industrialVocals.name: Sustained Note Wall Plugin
industrialVocals.p:
Use: long held notes that bloom into huge automated moments.

Prompt

Create a sustain-enhancement plugin called “Wall Bloom.” Start with 1176 into LA-2A serial compression, then add filtered plate and parallel distortion.
EQ: -2 dB at 320 Hz, +2 dB at 2.5 kHz, +2.5 dB at 6 kHz, shelf +1.5 dB at 12 kHz.
1176: ratio 4:1, attack 5 ms, release 80 ms, 4 dB GR.
LA-2A: 2–4 dB leveling.
Parallel distortion send: HPF 220 Hz, LPF 6.5 kHz, saturation Drive 18%, return at -15 dB.
Plate: 1.8 s decay, 28 ms pre-delay, HPF 300 Hz, LPF 7 kHz, 12% wet.
Macro knobs:

Bloom = raises plate send and parallel distortion return
Hold = increases LA-2A reduction and extends release feel
Presets: Long Cry, Chorus Hold, Wide Sustain.

Refine

“Shorten the tail and keep the held note more centered.”
“Make the sustain wider but still solo-voice.”

industrialVocals.name: Breath and Silence Automation Plugin
industrialVocals.p:
Use: “the vocal IS the production” moments, mutes, sharp entrances, dead stops.

Prompt

Create an automation-focused vocal plugin called “Silence to Impact.”
Add an intelligent gate with attack 1 ms, hold 35 ms, release 120 ms, threshold tuned so room tone disappears between phrases without chopping breath endings.
Add transient emphasis on phrase entries: +1.5 dB at 2.8 kHz for first 80 ms of each phrase.
Add optional phrase-end ducking: -1.5 dB over 90 ms before silence.
Add a reverse swell send option: 250 ms reverse tail, filtered 500 Hz to 6 kHz.
Macro knobs:

Cut Black = deepens gate and shortens release
Impact = increases phrase-entry transient presence and reverse swell
Presets: Hard Mute, Jump Cut Entry, Breath Edge.

Refine

“Make the gate less obvious.”
“More shock contrast between silence and entry.”

industrialVocals.name: Artifact Remover for Harsh AI/Digital Problems
industrialVocals.p:
Use: warble, fizz, watery highs, phasey edges, crunchy consonants.

Prompt

Create a restoration plugin called “Artifact Surgeon.” Blend spectral de-noise, dynamic resonance suppression, and phase repair.
Target zones: 2.7–4.3 kHz for harsh digital edge, 7.5–10.5 kHz for fizz, and above 12 kHz for phasey air smear.
Dynamic cuts should range from -2 dB to -6 dB depending on severity.
Add de-click for mouth ticks at 2–12 ms events.
Add low-end cleanup with HPF 65 Hz and sub-rumble gate below 50 Hz.
Add transient recovery so cleaned vocals do not go dull.
Macro knobs:

De-Warble = increases spectral smoothing and 2.7–4.3 kHz suppression
Restore Edge = adds transient recovery and eases top-end cuts
Presets: Phase Repair, Vocal De-Gunk, Digital Scar Cleanup.

Refine

“Keep the vocal bright; undo 1.5 dB of top-end reduction.”
“Focus more on watery highs than mid harshness.”

industrialVocals.name: Sibilance and Harshness Tamer
industrialVocals.p:
Use: loud belts and screams that stab too hard.

Prompt

Create a vocal dynamics plugin called “Needle Tamer.”
Add split-band control with one band at 5.5–7.2 kHz for sibilance and another at 2.8–4.6 kHz for scream harshness.
Sibilance band max reduction: -5 dB.
Harshness band max reduction: -3 dB.
Attack 0.5 ms, release 45 ms on sibilance; attack 5 ms, release 70 ms on harshness.
Add a post-band air shelf at 11.5 kHz +1 dB so de-essing doesn’t sound dull.
Macro knobs:

Tame S = deepens 5.5–7.2 kHz reduction
Smooth Rage = deepens 2.8–4.6 kHz reduction and lowers clipper drive
Presets: Sharp S Fix, Scream Smooth, Bright but Safe.

Refine

“Keep consonants aggressive but remove needle pain.”
“Only tame the top when he really leans in.”

industrialVocals.name: Full Auto-Pilot Vocal Brain
industrialVocals.p:
Use: one-plugin adaptive chain.

Prompt

Create a fully automatic vocal plugin called “Adaptive Male Vocal Brain.” It must listen to the incoming vocal and switch behavior between whisper, chest verse, aggressive verse, belt, and scream without manual intervention.
Internal clean chain should resemble U87 > 1073 > CL 1B.
Internal aggressive chain should resemble SM7B > 1176 > saturation.
The plugin must detect phrase intensity, spectral brightness, sibilance density, and sustain length.
Automatic rules:

if quiet/intimate: use HPF 70 Hz, soft opto compression, low room send
if chest verse: use HPF 75–85 Hz, 3:1 compression, slight 3 kHz push
if aggressive verse: engage saturation 10–16%, 4:1 compression, reduce 250–350 Hz
if belt: add dynamic harshness control at 3.8–5.5 kHz, plate 1.1–1.4 s
if scream: split-band saturation, low-pass highs around 9–10 kHz, deeper de-ess
Global knobs:
Intensity = more compression, saturation, and presence
Stability = more de-ess, artifact control, and transient management
Distance = dry/close to wider/processed
Presets: Auto Verse, Auto Full Range, Auto Scream Safe.
Keep it mono-compatible, chant-free, and studio-tight.

Refine

“Make the auto mode less bright in whispers.”
“Let the scream mode stay ugly, but stop the fizzy top.”

genreBlueprints.name: Pop Radio Vocal Chain
genreBlueprints.p: Build a vocal channel strip plugin. Stage 1: high-pass filter at 90 Hz, 12 dB/oct. Stage 2: subtractive EQ — cut 2.5 dB at 300 Hz (Q 1.4) for mud, cut 4 dB at 4.2 kHz (Q 3.0) for harshness. Stage 3: compressor like an LA-2A — slow optical attack (~10 ms), auto release, 3:1 ratio, 4–6 dB gain reduction. Stage 4: a second faster compressor like an 1176 at 4:1, attack 3 ms, release 250 ms, catching 2–3 dB peaks. Stage 5: air shelf +3 dB at 12 kHz like a Maag EQ4 "Air Band." Knobs: Body, De-Mud, Smooth, Air, Drive. Add a macro knob called "Radio" that simultaneously raises Air, tightens both compressors, and adds 5% parallel saturation. Presets: "Pop Radio," "Ballad Soft," "Dance Anthem."

genreBlueprints.name: Shimmer Halo" (pop vocal reverb)
genreBlueprints.p: Make a plate reverb like a vintage EMT 140 with pre-delay 80 ms, decay 1.8 s, low-cut at 250 Hz, high-cut at 9 kHz, plus a shimmer layer pitched +12 semitones at 20% blend. Knobs: Pre-Delay (0–200 ms), Decay (0.5–6 s), Shimmer, Width (0–150%), Duck (sidechained to input so reverb ducks 4 dB while vocal is active, releases in 300 ms). Presets: "Dua Halo," "Ballad Cathedral," "Tight Booth."

genreBlueprints.name: Slap & Throw Delay
genreBlueprints.p: Stereo delay: left 1/8 note, right 1/8 dotted, feedback 25%, ping-pong on. Filter the repeats: high-pass 400 Hz, low-pass 6 kHz, like a Roland Space Echo tape delay with 8% wow/flutter. Add a "Throw" button momentary mode for automating word-throws. Macro knob "Vibe": raises flutter, feedback, and saturation together. Presets: "Pop Slap 120 BPM," "Throw Ready," "Dreamy 1/4."

genreBlueprints.name: Glass Keys Enhancer" (for pop piano/keys)
genreBlueprints.p: EQ + chorus for keys: bell boost +2 dB at 5 kHz (Q 1.0), high shelf +1.5 dB at 10 kHz, chorus like a Roland Juno-60 (rate 0.8 Hz, depth 25%, stereo spread 100%). Knobs: Glass, Warmth (low shelf at 200 Hz, ±4 dB), Motion, Width. Preset: "Piano Ballad," "Synthwave Keys."

genreBlueprints.name: Pop Bass Glue
genreBlueprints.p: Bass plugin: mono below 120 Hz, saturation like an Ampeg tube preamp on 700 Hz–2 kHz only, compressor 4:1 with 30 ms attack / 100 ms release, sidechain input from the kick with 3 dB duck, release timed to 1/8 note at project BPM. Knobs: Sub Mono, Grit, Glue, Duck Depth.

genreBlueprints.name: Bus Finisher
genreBlueprints.p:
Mix-bus plugin like an SSL G-series bus compressor: ratio 2:1, attack 30 ms, release auto, 1–2 dB gain reduction, plus tape saturation like a Studer A800 at 15 ips, and a stereo widener above 8 kHz only. Macro knob "Finish" scales all three. Presets: "Pop Radio Glue," "EDM Pump" (release 0.1 s), "Gentle Ballad."

🔥 TRAP

genreBlueprints.name: Trap Ready Vocal Chain
genreBlueprints.p: Vocal chain: high-pass 100 Hz; hard autotune-style pitch correction, retune speed 0–10 ms, scale-locked; compressor like a CLA-76 all-buttons-in, attack 1 ms, release 200 ms, 6–8 dB GR; de-esser centered 6–8 kHz; presence boost +4 dB at 3 kHz; saturation like a distressor at 10% mix. Knobs: Tune Speed, Slam, Ess Control, Cut, Heat. Macro knob "Drip": increases autotune sharpness, presence, and stereo doubler width together. Presets: "Trap Ready," "Melodic Auto," "Aggressive Ad-Lib."

genreBlueprints.name: Dark Bounce Verb
genreBlueprints.p: Small dark room reverb — decay 0.6 s, pre-delay 20 ms, high-cut 4 kHz, like an old Lexicon PCM60 "small room" — plus a parallel 1/16-note slapback at 15% mix. Duck the wet signal 6 dB via sidechain from the dry vocal. Knobs: Room, Dark, Bounce, Duck. Presets: "Booth Tight," "Underwater Hook."

genreBlueprints.name: 808 Commander" ⭐ (the essential one)
genreBlueprints.p: Build an 808 processor: Stage 1 — glide/pitch snap control. Stage 2 — saturation like a driven Neve 1073 preamp adding harmonics at 60–250 Hz so the 808 reads on small speakers. Stage 3 — low shelf +3 dB at 45 Hz, tight high-pass at 25 Hz to remove rumble. Stage 4 — limiter with 0.1 ms lookahead. Sidechain input from kick, duck 5 dB, attack 0.5 ms, release 60 ms. Knobs: Sub, Knock (transient at 100–200 Hz), Grill (distortion), Phone (small-speaker harmonics), Tail (sustain envelope). Presets: "Memphis Knock," "Melodic Glide," "Distorted Rage."

genreBlueprints.name: Hi-Hat Machine
genreBlueprints.p: Hat processor: transient shaper +6 dB attack, high-pass 500 Hz, top-end exciter like an Aphex Aural Exciter above 10 kHz, auto-pan LFO synced to 1/16 notes with depth control, pitch knob ±12 semitones. Knobs: Snap, Sizzle, Travel, Pitch. Presets: "Rolls & Stutters," "Dark Hats."

genreBlueprints.name: Snare Crack
genreBlueprints.p: Snare/clap plugin: transient attack +8 dB (10 ms window), EQ bump +3 dB at 200 Hz (body) and +4 dB at 5 kHz (crack), short bright plate reverb 0.4 s decay, gated at -30 dB threshold like an 80s gated snare. Knobs: Body, Crack, Splash, Gate.

genreBlueprints.name: Dark Melody Texture
genreBlueprints.p:
For trap melodies (bells, keys, flutes): pitch wobble like a warped VHS tape (±8 cents, 0.3 Hz), low-pass at 8 kHz, vinyl noise layer at -35 dB, reverb 4 s decay 100% wet at 25% mix, sidechain-ducked to the 808. Knobs: Warp, Age, Ghost, Duck. Presets: "Memphis Phonk," "Ambient Trap."

🎙️ RAP (boom-bap / modern hip-hop)

genreBlueprints.name: Front & Center Rap Vocal
genreBlueprints.p: Rap vocal chain, minimal tuning: high-pass 80 Hz; EQ +2 dB at 120 Hz (chest), cut 3 dB at 400 Hz, +3 dB at 5 kHz (diction); compressor like an 1176 at 8:1, attack 5 ms, release 150 ms, 5 dB GR; parallel compression bus crushed 12 dB blended at 30%; tape saturation at 15%. Knobs: Chest, Clarity, Punch, Crush Blend, Tape. Macro "In Your Face": raises Punch + Crush + Clarity. Presets: "Boom Bap 90s," "Modern Clean," "Lo-Fi Mic."

genreBlueprints.name: Doubles & Ad-Lib Widener
genreBlueprints.p: Ad-lib plugin: micro-pitch doubler (±9 cents, 15 ms delay L/R) like an Eventide H3000 preset, telephone EQ mode (band-pass 800 Hz–3 kHz) on a toggle, pan spread knob. Knobs: Wide, Phone, Spread, Blend. Presets: "Stacked Hook," "Left-Right Ad-Libs."

genreBlueprints.name: Dusty Sampler" (boom-bap drums/samples)
genreBlueprints.p: Lo-fi processor like an SP-1200 / MPC60: 12-bit reduction, 26 kHz downsample, low-pass 7.5 kHz, vinyl crackle layer, slight swing-feel transient softening. Knobs: Bits, Dust, Filter, Era (morphs 1988→1995→2020). Presets: "SP Dust," "Golden Era," "Clean Modern."

genreBlueprints.name: Boom Bap Drum Bus
genreBlueprints.p: Drum bus: compressor like an API 2500 (ratio 4:1, attack 10 ms, release 100 ms, "thrust" HPF on detector at 100 Hz), +2 dB at 60 Hz, +2 dB at 8 kHz, parallel drive blend. Knobs: Slam, Boom, Snap, Blend. Presets: "Head Nod," "Hard NY."

genreBlueprints.name: Upright Bassline Warmer
genreBlueprints.p:
For rap basslines: like an LA-2A on bass — slow optical compression 3–5 dB GR, tube warmth at 80–200 Hz, mono-maker below 150 Hz. Knobs: Warm, Even, Mono. Preset: "Q-Tip Low End."

🕯️ INTIMATE (bedroom / acoustic / lo-fi soul)

genreBlueprints.name: Whisper Close Vocal
genreBlueprints.p: Intimate vocal chain: gentle high-pass at 70 Hz; proximity boost +2.5 dB at 180 Hz like singing close to a Neumann U47; compressor like an LA-2A, 2–3 dB GR only, slow and invisible; de-esser 7 kHz, gentle; breath enhancer (upward expansion above 8 kHz, +2 dB). NO hard tuning. Knobs: Close, Silk, Breath, Ease. Macro "Candlelight": adds warmth, softens the top, raises breath detail. Presets: "Bedroom 2AM," "Billie Whisper," "Acoustic Session."

genreBlueprints.name: Small Room Truth
genreBlueprints.p: Reverb like a real wooden room — convolution-style, decay 0.9 s, pre-delay 12 ms, early reflections prominent, high-cut 6 kHz. Second mode: spring reverb like a Fender tank at 20% mix. Knobs: Room Size, Wood, Spring, Distance. Presets: "Living Room," "Chapel Soft," "Tape Room."

genreBlueprints.name: Fingerpick Focus" (acoustic guitar)
genreBlueprints.p: Acoustic guitar plugin: cut 3 dB at 250 Hz (boom), notch -4 dB at 2.8 kHz (string squeak zone, Q 5), +2 dB at 10 kHz shimmer, compressor 2:1, attack 25 ms, release 200 ms, subtle tape flutter 0.2%. Knobs: De-Boom, Squeak Tame, Sparkle, Flutter. Presets: "Fingerstyle Close," "Strummed Wide."

genreBlueprints.name: Felt Piano Maker
genreBlueprints.p: Piano intimacy plugin: low-pass 6 kHz, mechanical key noise layer at -30 dB, tape wobble ±6 cents at 0.5 Hz, compressor squashing to 4 dB dynamic range like a heavily-limited Nils Frahm recording. Knobs: Felt, Mechanics, Wobble, Hug. Presets: "Felt & Tape," "Rainy Window."

genreBlueprints.name: "Wooden Room Lead Vocal" (folk)
genreBlueprints.p: Build a folk lead vocal chain for ONE solo voice only — no background vocals, no group vocals, no crowd, no audience ambience. High-pass 85 Hz; ribbon-mic tone like an RCA 77 (smooth roll-off above 12 kHz, warm 200 Hz lift); compressor like a Fairchild 670, 2:1, slow attack, 3 dB gain reduction; plate reverb 1.4 s decay, pre-delay 40 ms, 12% mix. Knobs: Ribbon, Round, Plate, Honesty (raw-signal blend 0–100%). Presets: "Solo Warm," "Harvest Close," "Solo Hall."

genreBlueprints.name: "Solo Double Blender" (folk/pop)
genreBlueprints.p: Create a single-voice thickener that never adds new voices — it only duplicates the existing dry vocal. Micro-pitch double at ±7 cents, 12 ms L / 18 ms R delay like an Eventide H3000 micro-shift, mid-side EQ (sides +2 dB at 3 kHz, mid untouched), width capped at 110%, bus compressor 2:1 slow glue, subtle tape hiss for era feel. Explicitly exclude: choir, chant, group vocal, crowd layers. Knobs: Double, Wide, Era, Glue. Presets: "Thick Solo," "Duet Illusion (still one singer)."

genreBlueprints.name: Banjo/Mandolin Tamer
genreBlueprints.p: Cut harsh pluck at 3.5 kHz (-4 dB, Q 3), body boost +2 dB at 300 Hz, fast compressor 4:1, attack 8 ms to catch pluck transients, spring reverb 15%. Knobs: Pluck Tame, Body, Boing, Sit Back.

genreBlueprints.name: Fiddle Silk
genreBlueprints.p: Violin/fiddle plugin: de-harsh dynamic EQ at 2.5–4 kHz (triggers above -18 dB), warm shelf +2 dB at 250 Hz, hall reverb 2.2 s like a stone church convolution. Knobs: Silk, Rosin, Hall, Distance.

genreBlueprints.name: "Studio Thump" (folk percussion)
genreBlueprints.p: Build a percussion weight plugin for close-miked studio drums only — no room crowd, no group claps, no live-audience character. Heavy parallel compression like smashed ribbon room mics (10:1, 20 dB GR, blended 40%), +3 dB at 80 Hz for low thump weight, transient shaper +4 dB attack in a 15 ms window, high-cut at 10 kHz to keep it dark and dry. Knobs: Thump, Smash, Dry Blend, Dark. Presets: "Floor Tom Weight," "Dry Kick Boom."

genreBlueprints.name: "Basement Fusion" (trap/pop/rock hybrid bus)
genreBlueprints.p: Build a hybrid bus plugin for a trap/pop/rock fusion — fully studio-produced character, zero live-audience or crowd ambience. Parallel path A: 808-style sub enhancer below 100 Hz. Parallel path B: guitar-amp distortion like a Marshall JCM800 applied only to 500 Hz–4 kHz. Path C: clean pop sheen — high shelf +3 dB at 11 kHz. Glue with an SSL-style bus compressor, 2:1, 30 ms attack, auto release. Sidechain pump synced to 1/4 notes, depth 0–8 dB. Knobs: Sub Riot, Amp Rage, Gloss, Glue, Pump. Macro knob "Polished↔Gritty" morphs from huge glossy studio (long verb, wide) to raw small (dry, distorted, mono-leaning). Presets: "Heavy Fusion," "Pop Punk 808," "Grunge Hook."

genreBlueprints.name: Hybrid Vocal Morph
genreBlueprints.p: One vocal plugin with a 3-way morph knob: position A = "Trap" (hard tune, dark short verb, slam compression), position B = "Pop" (light tune, plate shimmer, air +3 dB at 12 kHz), position C = "Rock" (no tune, tape drive, slap delay 110 ms like a Zeppelin vocal). Crossfade smoothly between all three. Add a "Scream Safe" limiter at the end. Presets: "Verse Trap→Hook Rock" (automatable morph), "All Gas."

genreBlueprints.name: Set-and-Forget AI Engineer
genreBlueprints.p: Create an intelligent auto-mixing plugin that listens to the incoming audio and adapts continuously. It should: (1) detect the source type (vocal, 808, drums, guitar, keys) and load the right processing chain automatically; (2) auto-detect the project key and BPM and sync all delay times and duck-release values to the tempo; (3) run auto-gain-staging to hit -18 dBFS average into each stage; (4) apply dynamic EQ that only cuts resonances when they ring (mud 200–400 Hz, harshness 2–5 kHz, sibilance 5–9 kHz); (5) auto-select reverb size based on song energy — small room in verses, bigger plate in hooks; (6) auto-ride the compressor to keep 4–6 dB GR on vocals and 2 dB on buses; (7) match the tonal balance to the genre it detects. Give me only four macro knobs: Amount (0–100% of all processing), Character (clean digital ↔ analog tape/console), Space (dry ↔ lush), and Loud (streaming-safe -14 LUFS target on/off). Presets: "Full Auto," "Auto But Gentle," "Auto Trap Bias," "Auto Folk Bias." Everything else, decide yourself by listening.

genreBlueprints.name: "Artifact Eraser" (the main one)
genreBlueprints.p: Build a restoration plugin that removes AI-generation artifacts from audio. Stage 1: spectral de-noise — learn the noise floor from the quietest 500 ms and subtract it, reduction 0–12 dB. Stage 2: de-swirl — detect and smooth metallic/watery phasing artifacts in the 2–8 kHz range using spectral smoothing, strength 0–100%. Stage 3: de-warble — pitch-stabilize wobbling sustained notes (correction window 50 ms, max ±15 cents). Stage 4: de-click/de-pop — remove transient glitches under 5 ms. Stage 5: aliasing cleaner — low-pass shimmer/fizz above 16 kHz with a smooth 24 dB/oct slope. Stage 6: mud-resonance suppressor — dynamic notch that only cuts 200–400 Hz when it rings above -20 dB. Knobs: De-Noise, De-Swirl, De-Warble, De-Click, De-Fizz, Focus. Macro knob "Restore" scales all six at once. Presets: "Vocal Rescue," "Full Mix Clean," "Gentle Polish," "Heavy Repair."

genreBlueprints.name: "Ghost Voice Mute" (kills phantom chants/backing vocals)
genreBlueprints.p: Create a plugin that detects and suppresses unwanted background vocal artifacts — ghost harmonies, faint chants, phantom crowd murmurs, and residual backing-vocal bleed — while preserving the main lead voice. Use center-channel isolation: keep the mid signal intact, apply spectral gating to the side channels in the 300 Hz–5 kHz vocal band, threshold -35 dB, attack 5 ms, release 200 ms. Add a "Lead Protect" detector that never touches audio when only one voice is present. Knobs: Ghost Mute (0–100%), Side Gate Threshold, Lead Protect, Air Keep (preserves side content above 8 kHz for width). Presets: "Solo Voice Only," "Mute Phantom Chants," "Light Cleanup."

genreBlueprints.name: "Tail Cleaner" (reverb/breath artifact edition)
genreBlueprints.p: Build a plugin that tightens smeared AI reverb tails and breath artifacts: downward expander below -45 dB with 2:1 ratio, 10 ms attack, 300 ms release; de-breath detector on 1–4 kHz noise bursts between phrases, reduction 0–10 dB; reverb-tail shortener that ducks the ambience 6 dB whenever the dry signal stops. Knobs: Tighten, De-Breath, Tail Cut, Natural (blend). Presets: "Dry It Up," "Keep It Human."

genreBlueprints.name: The Ultimate Pop Vocal Polish
genreBlueprints.p:
Plugin Idea: The Ultimate Pop Vocal Polish

The Prompt: "Create a custom vocal chain plugin that sounds like a Sony C800G microphone running into a Tube-Tech CL 1B compressor. Set the compressor to a 4:1 ratio, a quick 3ms attack, and a smooth 50ms release. Add a built-in EQ with a +3dB high shelf at exactly 10kHz for air, and a -2dB cut at 400Hz to remove mud. Create a macro knob called 'Sheen & Squeeze' that simultaneously increases the high shelf and lowers the compressor threshold. Include named presets: 'Pop Radio', 'Dua Whisper', and 'Solo Studio Lead'." (Replaced "Boyband" to prevent gang vocals)
Iteration Prompt (if needed): "Make the saturation warmer by rolling off the absolute highs above 12kHz, and make the 'Sheen' macro a bit less aggressive."

genreBlueprints.name: Sub-Harmonic 808 Destroyer
genreBlueprints.p:
Plugin Idea: Sub-Harmonic 808 Destroyer

The Prompt: "Build an 808 enhancer plugin modeled after a Thermionic Culture Vulture saturator blended with a dbx 120A subharmonic synthesizer. The sub-synth must target the 30Hz–60Hz frequency range. Include a 'Drive' knob that scales from 1% to 100% introducing 2nd and 3rd order harmonics. Create a macro knob named '808 Melt' that turns up the drive while slightly lowering the master output to volume-match. Include named presets: 'Trap Ready', 'Atlanta Sub', and 'Blown Trunk'."
Iteration Prompt (if needed): "Add a sidechain input linked to the kick drum so the 808 automatically ducks by -6dB with a fast 10ms attack and 40ms release every time the kick hits."

genreBlueprints.name: Boom-Bap In-Your-Face Compressor
genreBlueprints.p:
Plugin Idea: Boom-Bap In-Your-Face Compressor

The Prompt: "Generate a vocal compressor plugin that mimics an aggressive Urei 1176 with 'all buttons in', running through a vintage Neve 1073 preamp. Set default parameters to a lightning-fast attack (<1ms) and a fast release (50ms). Add an EQ module boosting +2.5dB at 5kHz for vocal presence. Add a single macro knob called 'Aggression' that pushes the preamp input gain while dropping the compressor threshold. Give me presets called '90s Boom Bap', 'Modern Drill', and 'Dry Center Vocal'." (Replaced "Hype/Ad-lib" to prevent background shouting)
Iteration Prompt (if needed): "Slow the attack down to 3ms to let the sharp consonants of the rap delivery punch through before the compression clamps down."

genreBlueprints.name: ASMR Breath & Proximity Enhancer
genreBlueprints.p:
Plugin Idea: ASMR Breath & Proximity Enhancer

The Prompt: "Design a vocal processor for intimate vocals. I want it to sound like a Neumann U47 tube mic into an optical LA-2A style compressor. It must include a dynamic EQ that automatically dips -3dB precisely between 4.5kHz and 7kHz only when sharp sibilance hits. Set the compressor to a slow 10ms attack to let breaths through. Add a macro knob named 'Proximity Effect' that gently boosts 120Hz while bringing up the noise floor with a subtle analog tape hiss. Presets: 'Bedtime Whisper', 'Isolated Whisper Room', and 'Raw Takes'." (Replaced "Coffeehouse" to prevent background chatter/live audience noise)
Iteration Prompt (if needed): "The tape hiss is too loud. Turn the noise floor down by -12dB and make the tape saturation warmer and darker."

genreBlueprints.name: Acoustic Wood & Resonance Reverb
genreBlueprints.p:
Plugin Idea: Acoustic Wood & Resonance Reverb

The Prompt: "Create an acoustic guitar plugin that combines a Pultec EQP-1A style equalizer with a vintage EMT 140 Plate Reverb. On the EQ side, boost 100Hz for body and 8kHz for string shimmer simultaneously. Set the plate reverb decay to 1.2 seconds, with a pre-delay of 25ms to separate the initial string pluck from the reverb tail. Add a macro knob called 'Wood Room Resonance' that controls the wet/dry mix and the EQ boosts at the same time. Include presets: 'Indie Folk', 'Appalachian Strings', and 'Dry Acoustic Cabin'." (Replaced "Campfire" to prevent sing-alongs and crackling fire noise)
Iteration Prompt (if needed): "Lengthen the pre-delay to 45ms and roll off the low frequencies of the reverb tail below 250Hz so the mix doesn't get muddy."

genreBlueprints.name: The Genre-Bender Bus Strip
genreBlueprints.p:
Plugin Idea: The Genre-Bender Bus Strip

The Prompt: "Create a hybrid mix bus plugin combining Trap, Pop, and Rock elements. It should behave like a Distressor compressor (6:1 ratio, 5ms attack, 100ms release) routed into a Marshall JCM800 cabinet simulator, finishing with a Lexicon 224 hall reverb (0.8s decay). Add an EQ with a drastic scoop of -4dB at 400Hz and a wide boost of +3dB at 3kHz. Give me a macro knob called 'Tight Control' that increases overdrive distortion, widens the stereo image by 15% above 5kHz, and shortens the reverb decay. Presets: 'Pop-Punk Trap', 'Studio 808 Rock', and 'Tight Hybrid Crush'." (Replaced "Stadium", "Mosh", and "Riot" to prevent live crowd chants and cheering)
Iteration Prompt (if needed): "Bypass the cabinet simulator on frequencies below 150Hz so the Trap 808s and subs stay clean and don't distort."

genreBlueprints.name: The Sentient Mastering Engineer
genreBlueprints.p:
Plugin Idea: The Sentient Mastering Engineer

The Prompt: "Create a sentient mastering plugin that runs entirely on auto-pilot. I want it to listen to the incoming audio in real-time, automatically identify the BPM and frequency balance, and dynamically adjust an internal SSL-style bus compressor (auto-release, 1.5:1 ratio), a FabFilter-style dynamic EQ to tame resonant harshness, and a true-peak limiter. It should feature only two main macro knobs: 'Loudness Target' (measured in LUFS from -14 to -7) and 'Spectral Balance' (sweeping from Dark/Warm to Bright/Modern). Include a preset called 'Auto-Magic'."
Iteration Prompt (if needed): "It sounds too squashed. Ease up the limiting threshold by 2dB, slow down the SSL compressor attack to 30ms to let the transients breathe, and prioritize keeping the snare drum punchy."

genreBlueprints.name: AI Audio Purifier
genreBlueprints.p:
The Prompt: "Create an audio restoration plugin modeled after a hybrid of iZotope RX Spectral De-noise and a Soothe2 dynamic resonance suppressor. Set it to automatically identify and dynamically cut -6dB of digital harshness in the 2.5kHz to 4kHz range, and remove high-frequency phase artifacts above 12kHz. Add a multi-band noise gate targeting frequencies below 200Hz with a fast 1ms attack and 200ms release to clean up low-end rumble. Create a macro knob called 'Artifact Cleanse' that simultaneously increases the depth of the dynamic EQ cuts and tightens the noise gate. Include named presets: 'De-Warble', 'Vocal De-Gunk', and 'Phase Repair'."

productionGuides.name: Solo male studio footer
productionGuides.p: One solo male lead vocalist only, recorded in a controlled studio. No crowd, audience, choir, gang vocals, chants, group shouts, unison responses, call-and-response, sing-along passages, applause, stage bleed, concert ambience, or live-room wash. Avoid “hey,” “oh,” “whoa,” and audience-cue phrases. Do not generate additional singers. Any doubling must be made from the same dry lead through micro-delay or pitch shifting. Stable formants, complete consonants, clean phrase endings, no ghost syllables, watery phasing, metallic smear, digital warble, or phantom backing vocals.

productionGuides.name: Industrial vocal suite and automation directions
productionGuides.p:
If you want one giant prompt that asks for the whole pack at once, use this:

Create a complete male vocal plugin suite for a 1990s industrial/alternative rock tenor/high-baritone with Chicago/Cleveland energy. Build separate plugins for: close whisper intro, warm chest verse, aggressive midrange verse, high-baritone grit, tenor belt chorus, distorted scream, falsetto/head voice lift, low octave support, tight double tracker, robotic pitch layer, telephone/PA bridge, sustained note wall, breath and silence automation, artifact remover, sibilance/harshness tamer, and full auto-pilot vocal brain.

Include exact EQ frequencies, Q values, compressor ratios, attack/release times, saturation drive amounts, delay times, reverb decay and pre-delay values, and knob names.
Reference real sonic archetypes like 1176, LA-2A, Neve 1073, CL 1B, Distressor, SansAmp, EMT 140, Lexicon hall.
Add macro knobs that control multiple parameters at once.
Add named presets for every plugin.
Design all processing for single-voice, studio-isolated male vocals only.
No crowd, no chants, no gang vocals, no singalong layers, no audience ambience, no choir bloom.
The sound should move from warm and intimate in quiet parts to harsh, cut-forward, distorted, and dramatic in loud parts, with extreme automation, intentional silence, industrial texture, and no accidental mess.
